abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate personalized recommendations without task-specific training, but changing a protected attribute while holding interaction history fixed can alter the semantic content of recommended items. We study fairness control when model weights and full-vocabulary logits are unavailable. We propose Fair- Rec, an item-level decoding framework that uses an offline-calibrated semantic-disparity threshold and controls candidate selection as recommendation lists are generated. A hard variant filters candidates against the threshold; a soft variant trades off candidate likelihood and disparity while adapting a penalty using observed violations. Under an explicit uniform enforceability assumption, we establish a pathwise O(1/T) upper bound on the excess empirical violation rate of the soft decoder. Experiments on MovieLens-1M and Amazon Movies & TV using Qwen3-8B and Llama3.1-8B-Instruct show that the soft variant lowers measured counterfactual disparity relative to zero- =shot recommendation, UP5, and FACTER, while retaining competitive HR@10 and NDCG@10.

ob.ai_reason: 核心为LLM推荐公平性，属推荐系统研究
ob.tldr: 针对LLM推荐在无法访问模型权重和完整词表概率时难以控制公平性的问题，Fair-Rec以离线校准的语义差异阈值进行候选解码，并设计自适应软惩罚机制；实验显示，该方法可降低反事实差异，同时保持有竞争力的HR@10与NDCG@10。

title: Conformal Fair Decoding for Large Language Model Recommenders
title_zh: 面向大语言模型推荐器的保形公平解码
